The project

From an idea to something useful.

I designed, built, and iterated a rescue-drone prototype to explore how aerial systems can support emergency supply delivery and search and rescue. I focused on stability, endurance, payload performance, control response, and communication reliability.

60Laboratory flights
3Outdoor field trials
20–30 minReported flight time
~3 kmReported RC range
01

Build and integrate

I developed the mechanical and electrical prototype, connecting flight control, camera-based perception, and a ground station. The report documents the architecture and software workflow below.

02

Test and revise

I completed 60 laboratory test flights and three outdoor field trials in Vung Tau and Dong Nai, using observations from each round to guide revisions.

03

Connect perception and response

The system combines person detection, pose analysis, and time-based alert logic with map-based telemetry to support rescue coordination.

Current scope

The project also explored extended control through 4G connectivity. The drone remains a prototype; the reported operating figures describe the development work rather than a guaranteed rescue capability.

Engineering in detail

From camera input to a rescue alert

The report connects mechanical design, flight control, onboard vision, and a ground-station interface into one prototype. The central engineering problem is turning a moving camera’s observations into an actionable location alert.

Airframe & flight

An F650-based quadcopter modeled in SolidWorks combines a Pixhawk flight controller, GPS and inertial sensing, a Raspberry Pi, and a camera. The report describes PID attitude control, GPS-waypoint missions, and return-to-home landing.

Perception & tracking

YOLOv5 identifies people, SORT maintains tracks across frames, and MediaPipe Pose estimates body landmarks for each tracked person.

Behavior over time

The software examines an arm raised above the head, wrist movement, and elbow-angle changes. A timed state machine escalates persistent trigger conditions instead of relying on one video frame.

Operator interface

A Flask application with SocketIO brings together live video, a Leaflet map, waypoints, flight telemetry, and location alerts. The report describes mission pausing and coordinate transmission after an SOS trigger.

How the alert logic works

  1. Detect & follow

    Find people in the camera feed and maintain a track for each person.

  2. Inspect the pose

    Compare wrist and head positions; calculate motion features from recent observations.

  3. Require persistence

    The report’s intermediate FROZEN state begins after 1.5 seconds; SOS begins after 3 seconds of a persistent trigger. These are software settings for the prototype.

  4. Inform the operator

    Display the alert state and relay location information to the monitoring station for human follow-up.

What the report evaluates

Chapter 5 reports the following observations. The report does not supply the raw evaluation dataset, sample counts, or a complete test protocol, so these figures are presented as report-stated results.

Reported observationValue in the reportEvaluation context
GPS waypoint followingTypical path deviation under 0.6 mChapter 5 describes comparison with the planned GPS path using telemetry and mapped flight tracks.
Person detectionOver 95% in controlled testsReported for controlled person-detection tests using the vision and tracking pipeline.
Distress recognitionFalse-positive rate below 5%Reported for the pose-and-time-based distress-recognition logic; separate from person detection.

Questions guiding the next iteration

The report identifies crowded scenes, weather and visibility, battery life, and onboard computation as constraints. A stronger evaluation would separate person detection from distress recognition, record false alarms across different conditions, and document the tested payload configuration.

Technical description: Rescue Drone Project Report, Chapters 3–6 and Figures 34–36.

Field testing & demonstration

From coastal trials to shared learning

Testing the drone above coastal water, presenting the assembled prototype, and sharing the field setup with students.

In pictures

Further details

Flight performance

The prototype achieved 20–30 minutes of flight time and an approximately 3 km RC range, with extended control explored through 4G connectivity.

Payload design limit

The technical report sets a maximum cargo weight of 5 kg within the project’s design scope. This is the documented design limit, rather than a measured payload result.
